questions.text: During the melting of a slab of ice at 273 K at atmospheric pressure :

options.label: A
options.text: Internal energy of ice-water system remains unchanged.

options.label: B
options.text: Positive work is done by the ice-water system on the atmosphere.

options.label: C
options.text: Internal energy of the ice-water system decreases.

options.label: D
options.text: Positive work is done on the ice-water system by the atmosphere.

questions.solution: During melting of ice, its volume decreases (as ice is less dense than liquid water). Therefore, \Delta V < 0, meaning work done by system W = P\Delta V < 0, so positive work is done on the ice-water system by the atmosphere. Also, heat is absorbed (\Delta Q > 0), so by first law \Delta U = \Delta Q - W > 0 (internal energy increases).

questions.text: Consider a completely full cylindrical water tank of height 1.6 m and cross-sectional area 0.5 m^2. It has a small hole in its side at a height 90 cm from the bottom. Assume, the cross-sectional area of the hole to be negligibly small as compared to that of the water tank. If a load 50 kg is applied at the top surface of the water in the tank then the velocity of the water coming out at the instant when the hole is opened is : (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.solution:
Applying Bernoulli's equation between top surface (1) and hole (2) (with datum at hole level, height difference h = 160 - 90 = 70\text{ cm} = 0.7\text{ m}):
P_0 + \frac{mg}{A} + \rho gh = P_0 + \frac{1}{2}\rho v_2^2
\frac{50 \times 10}{0.5} + 10^3 \times 10 \times 0.7 = \frac{1}{2} \times 10^3 v_2^2
1000 + 7000 = 500 v_2^2 \implies 8000 = 500 v_2^2 \implies v_2^2 = 16 \implies v_2 = 4\text{ m/s}.

questions.text:
A parallel plate capacitor is filled equally (half) with two dielectrics of dielectric constant \varepsilon_1 and \varepsilon_2, as shown in figures. The distance between the plates is d and area of each plate is A. If capacitance in first configuration and second configuration are C_1 and C_2 respectively, then \frac{C_1}{C_2} is :

![Capacitor Configurations](question-images/jee-2025/03-apr-morning-2025/q8_diagram.png)
questions.solution:
First configuration (series combination of two capacitors with thickness d/2, area A):
C = \frac{2\varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_0 A}{d}, C' = \frac{2\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_0 A}{d}
C_1 = \frac{C C'}{C + C'} = \frac{2\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_0 A}{d(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2)} = \frac{2\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2}{\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2} C_0

Second configuration (parallel combination of two capacitors with thickness d, area A/2):
C_2 = \frac{\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_0 (A/2)}{d} + \frac{\varepsilon_2 \varepsilon_0 (A/2)}{d} = \frac{(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2)}{2} C_0

Thus, \frac{C_1}{C_2} = \frac{2\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2 C_0 / (\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2)}{(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2) C_0 / 2} = \frac{4\varepsilon_1 \varepsilon_2}{(\varepsilon_1 + \varepsilon_2)^2}.

A force of 49 N acts tangentially at the highest point of a sphere (solid) of mass 20 kg, kept on a rough horizontal plane. If the sphere rolls without slipping, then the acceleration of the center of the sphere is

![Sphere with Force](question-images/jee-2025/03-apr-morning-2025/q10_diagram.png)

Taking torque about the point of contact with the ground (bottom point):
\tau = F \times 2r = I_{\text{bottom}} \alpha = (\frac{2}{5}mr^2 + mr^2) \alpha = \frac{7}{5}mr^2 \alpha

questions.text:
A piston of mass M is hung from a massless spring whose restoring force law goes as F = -kx^3, where k is the spring constant of appropriate dimension. The piston separates the vertical chamber into two parts, where the bottom part is filled with 'n' moles of an ideal gas. An external work is done on the gas isothermally (at a constant temperature T) with the help of a heating filament (with negligible volume) mounted in lower part of the chamber, so that the piston goes up from a height L_0 to L_1, the total energy delivered by the filament is (Assume spring to be in its natural length before heating)

![Piston in Cylinder](question-images/jee-2025/03-apr-morning-2025/q11_diagram.png)
questions.solution:
By Work-Energy Theorem / First Law of Thermodynamics for isothermal expansion (\Delta U = 0):
Total heat / energy delivered Q = W_{\text{gas}} + \Delta U_{\text{grav}} + \Delta U_{\text{spring}}
W_{\text{gas}} = nRT \ln(\frac{V_1}{V_0}) = nRT \ln(\frac{A L_1}{A L_0}) = nRT \ln(\frac{L_1}{L_0})
\Delta U_{\text{grav}} = Mg(L_1 - L_0)
\Delta U_{\text{spring}} = \int_{L_0}^{L_1} k x^3 dx = \frac{k}{4}(L_1^4 - L_0^4)
Total energy = nRT \ln(\frac{L_1}{L_0}) + Mg(L_1 - L_0) + \frac{k}{4}(L_1^4 - L_0^4).

questions.text: A gas is kept in a container having walls which are thermally non-conducting. Initially the gas has a volume of 800 cm^3 and temperature 27^\circ\text{C}. The change in temperature when the gas is adiabatically compressed to 200 cm^3 is : (Take \gamma = 1.5 : \gamma is the ratio of specific heats at constant pressure and at constant volume)
questions.solution:
Initial state: V_1 = 800\text{ cm}^3, T_1 = 27^\circ\text{C} = 300\text{ K}, \gamma = 1.5.
For adiabatic process, T V^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}.
T_2 = T_1 (\frac{V_1}{V_2})^{\gamma - 1} = 300 (\frac{800}{200})^{1.5 - 1} = 300 \times (4)^{0.5} = 300 \times 2 = 600\text{ K}.
Change in temperature \Delta T = T_2 - T_1 = 600 - 300 = 300\text{ K}.

questions.text: The electrostatic potential on the surface of uniformly charged spherical shell of radius R = 10 cm is 120 V. The potential at the centre of shell, at a distance r = 5 cm from centre, and at a distance r = 15 cm from the centre of the shell respectively, are :
questions.solution:
For a conducting spherical shell:
Inside the shell (r \le R), potential is constant and equal to surface potential: V = 120\text{ V}.
Therefore at centre (r = 0) and at r = 5 cm: V = 120\text{ V}.
Outside the shell (r = 15 cm > R = 10 cm):
V(r) = \frac{kQ}{r} = \frac{kQ}{R} \cdot \frac{R}{r} = 120 \times \frac{10}{15} = 80\text{ V}.

questions.text: A particle is released from height S above the surface of the earth. At certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of the earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively.
questions.solution:
Let height above surface be x. Potential energy PE = mgx. Distance fallen = S - x, so KE = \frac{1}{2}m v^2 = mg(S - x).
Given KE = 3 PE \implies mg(S - x) = 3 mgx \implies S - x = 3x \implies x = \frac{S}{4}.
Speed v = \sqrt{2g(S - x)} = \sqrt{2g(\frac{3S}{4})} = \sqrt{\frac{3gS}{2}}.

questions.text:
Consider following statements for refraction of light through prism, when angle of deviation is minimum.
(A) The refracted ray inside prism becomes parallel to the base.
(B) Larger angle prisms provide smaller angle of minimum deviation.
(C) Angle of incidence and angle of emergence becomes equal.
(D) There are always two sets of angle of incidence for which deviation will be same except at minimum deviation setting.
(E) Angle of refraction becomes double of prism angle.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
At minimum deviation (\delta = \delta_m):
- i = e (Angle of incidence equals angle of emergence, statement C is correct).
- The refracted ray inside the prism is parallel to the base (statement A is correct).
- For any deviation \delta > \delta_m, there are two distinct angles of incidence giving the same deviation, except at \delta_m where they merge into one (statement D is correct).
- At minimum deviation, r = A/2 (not double, statement E is false).
Hence, A, C and D only.

questions.text: Three identical spheres of mass m, are placed at the vertices of an equilateral triangle of length a. When released, they interact only through gravitational force and collide after a time T = 4 seconds. If the sides of the triangle are increased to length 2a and also the masses of the spheres are made 2m, then they will collide after ________ seconds.
questions.solution:
By dimensional analysis / Kepler's third law scaling for gravitational collapse:
T \propto \sqrt{\frac{a^3}{G m}}
When length becomes a' = 2a and mass becomes m' = 2m:
T' = T \sqrt{\frac{(2)^3}{2}} = 4 \times \sqrt{4} = 4 \times 2 = 8\text{ s}.

questions.text: Two coherent monochromatic light beams of intensities 4I and 9I are superimposed. The difference between the maximum and minimum intensities in the resulting interference pattern is xI. The value of x is ________.
questions.solution:
I_{\max} = (\sqrt{I_1} + \sqrt{I_2})^2 = (\sqrt{4I} + \sqrt{9I})^2 = (2\sqrt{I} + 3\sqrt{I})^2 = (5\sqrt{I})^2 = 25I
I_{\min} = (\sqrt{I_2} - \sqrt{I_1})^2 = (3\sqrt{I} - 2\sqrt{I})^2 = I
I_{\max} - I_{\min} = 25I - I = 24I \implies x = 24.

questions.text:
A loop ABCDA, carrying current I = 12 A, is placed in a plane, consists of two semi-circular segments of radius R_1 = 6\pi m and R_2 = 4\pi m. The magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at center O is k \times 10^{-7} T. The value of k is ________.

(Given \mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1})

![Loop ABCDA](question-images/jee-2025/03-apr-morning-2025/q24_diagram.png)
questions.solution:
Straight segments AB and CD point radially toward/away from O, so their magnetic field at O is 0.
For the semicircular arcs carrying opposite circular directions:
B_0 = |B_{R_2} - B_{R_1}| = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4 R_2} - \frac{\mu_0 I}{4 R_1} = \frac{\mu_0 I}{4} (\frac{1}{4\pi} - \frac{1}{6\pi}) = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 12}{4} \times \frac{1}{12\pi} = 12\pi \times 10^{-7} \times \frac{1}{12\pi} = 1 \times 10^{-7}\text{ T}.
Thus k = 1.

questions.text: Which of the following postulate of Bohr's model of hydrogen atom in not in agreement with quantum mechanical model of an atom ?

Parametric line through P(\sqrt{5},\sqrt{5}): x = \sqrt{5} + r\cos\theta, y = \sqrt{5} + r\sin\theta.
Substituting into ellipse gives quadratic in r: r^2(25\cos^2\theta + 36\sin^2\theta) + 2\sqrt{5}r(25\cos\theta + 36\sin\theta) - 595 = 0.
Product of distances PA \cdot PB = |r_1 r_2| = \frac{595}{25 + 11\sin^2\theta}.
This product is maximum when \sin^2\theta = 0 \implies \theta = 0 (line is parallel to x-axis, y = \sqrt{5}).
For y = \sqrt{5}: \frac{x^2}{36} + \frac{5}{25} = 1 \implies x^2 = 36(1 - 1/5) = 36 \times \frac{4}{5} = \frac{144}{5} \implies x = \pm \frac{12}{\sqrt{5}}.

Therefore, 5(PA^2 + PB^2) = 338.

questions.text: Let g be a differentiable function such that \int_0^x g(t) dt = x - \int_0^x t g(t) dt, x \ge 0 and let y = y(x) satisfy the differential equation \frac{dy}{dx} - y\tan x = 2(x+1)\sec x g(x), x \in [0, \frac{\pi}{2}). If y(0) = 0, then y(\frac{\pi}{3}) is equal to
questions.solution:
Differentiating \int_0^x g(t) dt = x - \int_0^x t g(t) dt w.r.t. x by Leibniz rule:
g(x) = 1 - x g(x) \implies g(x)(1+x) = 1 \implies g(x) = \frac{1}{1+x}.
The differential equation becomes:
\frac{dy}{dx} - y\tan x = 2(x+1)\sec x (\frac{1}{x+1}) = 2\sec x.
Integrating factor \text{IF} = e^{-\int \tan x dx} = e^{\ln|\cos x|} = \cos x.
y \cos x = \int 2\sec x \cos x dx = \int 2 dx = 2x + C.
Given y(0) = 0 \implies C = 0 \implies y = 2x \sec x.
At x = \pi/3: y(\frac{\pi}{3}) = 2(\frac{\pi}{3}) \sec(\frac{\pi}{3}) = \frac{2\pi}{3} \times 2 = \frac{4\pi}{3}.

questions.text: Let the domain of the function f(x) = \log_2 \log_4 \log_6 (3 + 4x - x^2) be (a, b). If \int_0^{b-a} [x^2]\ dx = p - \sqrt{q} - \sqrt{r}, p,q,r \in \mathbb{N}, \gcd(p, q, r) = 1, where [\cdot] is the greatest integer function, then p + q + r is equal to

questions.solution:
The parabolas are symmetric about the line y = x.
The tangent at the point of closest approach must have slope m = 1.
For y = x^2 + 2: \frac{dy}{dx} = 2x = 1 \implies x = \frac{1}{2}, y = \frac{1}{4} + 2 = \frac{9}{4}.
Point on first parabola is B(1/2, 9/4), and on second is A(9/4, 1/2).
Distance AB = \sqrt{(\frac{9}{4} - \frac{1}{2})^2 + (\frac{1}{2} - \frac{9}{4})^2} = \sqrt{2(\frac{7}{4})^2} = \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{4}.
The smallest circle touching both parabolas has AB as its diameter, so its radius = \frac{AB}{2} = \frac{7\sqrt{2}}{8}.

questions.solution:
Left hand limit: \lim_{x \to 0^-} (1+ax)^{1/x} = e^a.

Right hand limit: \lim_{x \to 0^+} \frac{\sqrt{x+4}-2}{(x+c)^{1/3}-2}.
For limit to exist, indeterminate form 0/0 requires c^{1/3} - 2 = 0 \implies c = 8.
Using L'Hopital's rule at x = 0:
\lim_{x \to 0^+} \frac{\frac{1}{2\sqrt{x+4}}}{\frac{1}{3}(x+8)^{-2/3}} = \frac{1/4}{\frac{1}{3}(8)^{-2/3}} = \frac{1/4}{\frac{1}{3 \times 4}} = 3.
Continuity requires e^a = 1 + b = 3 \implies e^a = 3, b = 2, c = 8.
Thus e^a b c = 3 \times 2 \times 8 = 48.

Vector PQ = (-3, 4, t-4). Since PQ \perp L_1 (direction (0,0,1)), t - 4 = 0 \implies t = 4.
Foot of perpendicular is Q(1, 2, 7).
Square of distance PQ^2 = (4-1)^2 + (-2-2)^2 + (7-7)^2 = 3^2 + (-4)^2 = 9 + 16 = 25.

questions.text: All five letter words are made using all the letters A, B, C, D, E and arranged as in an English dictionary with serial numbers. Let the word at serial number n be denoted by W_n. Let the probability P(W_n) of choosing the word W_n satisfy P(W_n) = 2P(W_{n-1}), n > 1. If P(\text{CDBEA}) = \frac{2^\alpha}{2^\beta - 1}, \alpha, \beta \in \mathbb{N}, then \alpha + \beta is equal to : ________
questions.solution:
Total words = 5! = 120.
P(W_n) = 2^{n-1} P(W_1) = 2^{n-1} x.
\sum_{i=1}^{120} P(W_i) = x(1 + 2 + \dots + 2^{119}) = x(2^{120} - 1) = 1 \implies x = \frac{1}{2^{120} - 1}.
Rank of CDBEA:
- Starting with A: 4! = 24
- Starting with B: 4! = 24
- Starting with CA: 3! = 6
- Starting with CB: 3! = 6
- Starting with CDA: 2! = 2
- CDBAE: 1
- CDBEA: 1
Total rank n = 24 + 24 + 6 + 6 + 2 + 1 + 1 = 64.
P(W_{64}) = 2^{63} x = \frac{2^{63}}{2^{120} - 1}.
Thus \alpha = 63, \beta = 120 \implies \alpha + \beta = 63 + 120 = 183.

questions.text: Let the product of the focal distances of the point P(4, 2\sqrt{3}) on the hyperbola H : \frac{x^2}{a^2} - \frac{y^2}{b^2} = 1 be 32. Let the length of the conjugate axis of H be p and the length of its latus rectum be q. Then p^2 + q^2 is equal to ________
questions.solution:
For point P(x_1, y_1) on hyperbola, focal distances are |a e \pm x_1|, and PS_1 \cdot PS_2 = (a e + x_1)(a e - x_1) = a^2 e^2 - x_1^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 16 = 32 \implies a^2 + b^2 = 48.
P(4, 2\sqrt{3}) lies on hyperbola: \frac{16}{a^2} - \frac{12}{b^2} = 1 \implies 16b^2 - 12a^2 = a^2 b^2.
Substitute b^2 = 48 - a^2:
16(48 - a^2) - 12a^2 = a^2(48 - a^2) \implies 768 - 28a^2 = 48a^2 - a^4 \implies a^4 - 76a^2 + 768 = 0.
Factoring: (a^2 - 64)(a^2 - 12) = 0. Since a^2 < 48, a^2 = 12 \implies b^2 = 36.
(Or with PS_1 \cdot PS_2 = (ex_1)^2 - a^2 = (4e)^2 - a^2 = 16e^2 - a^2):
16(1 + b^2/a^2) - a^2 = 32 \implies b^2 - a^2 = 4 \implies a^2 = 8, b^2 = 12.
Conjugate axis p = 2b \implies p^2 = 4b^2 = 4(12) = 48.
Latus rectum q = \frac{2b^2}{a} \implies q^2 = \frac{4b^4}{a^2} = \frac{4(144)}{8} = 72.
Thus p^2 + q^2 = 48 + 72 = 120.

questions.text: Let \vec{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}, \vec{b} = 3\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} - \hat{k}, \vec{c} = \lambda\hat{j} + \mu\hat{k} and \hat{d} be a unit vector such that \vec{a}\times\hat{d} = \vec{b}\times\hat{d} and \vec{c}\cdot\hat{d} = 1. If \vec{c} is perpendicular to \vec{a}, then |3\lambda\hat{d} + \mu\vec{c}|^2 is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
(\vec{a} - \vec{b}) \times \hat{d} = 0 \implies \hat{d} = t(\vec{a} - \vec{b}) = t(-2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 2\hat{k}).
Since |\hat{d}| = 1 \implies |t|\sqrt{4+1+4} = 3|t| = 1 \implies |t| = 1/3.
\vec{c} \perp \vec{a} \implies (0, \lambda, \mu) \cdot (1, 1, 1) = \lambda + \mu = 0 \implies \mu = -\lambda.
\vec{c} = \lambda(\hat{j} - \hat{k}) \implies |\vec{c}|^2 = 2\lambda^2.
\vec{c} \cdot \hat{d} = 1 \implies \lambda(0, 1, -1) \cdot t(-2, -1, 2) = 1 \implies -3\lambda t = 1 \implies \lambda^2 t^2 = 1/9 \implies \lambda^2 = 1.
|3\lambda\hat{d} + \mu\vec{c}|^2 = 9\lambda^2|\hat{d}|^2 + \mu^2|\vec{c}|^2 + 6\lambda\mu(\hat{d}\cdot\vec{c})
= 9(1)(1) + (1)(2) + 6(1)(-1)(1) = 9 + 2 - 6 = 5.

questions.text: If the number of seven-digit numbers, such that the sum of their digits is even, is m \cdot 10^n ; m, n \in \lbrace 1, 2, 3, \dots, 9 \rbrace, then m + n is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
Total 7-digit numbers = 9 \times 10^6 = 9000000.
For any choice of the first 6 digits (which can be chosen in 9 \times 10^5 ways), the sum of the first 6 digits is either even or odd. In either case, exactly 5 of the 10 possible choices for the 7th digit (last digit) will make the total sum of 7 digits even.
Total numbers with even digit sum = 9 \times 10^5 \times 5 = 45 \times 10^5 = 4.5 \times 10^6 = 9 \times 5 \times 10^5 = 45 \times 10^5 = 9 \times 500000 = 9 \times 5 \times 10^5 \implies m = 9, n = 5.
Thus m + n = 9 + 5 = 14.

questions.text: The area of the region bounded by the curve y = \max(|x|, x|x-2|), then x-axis and the lines x = -2 and x = 4 is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
Analyze f(x) = \max(|x|, x|x-2|) on [-2, 4]:
- For x \in [-2, 0]: |x| = -x, x|x-2| = x(2-x) = 2x - x^2 \le 0. So \max is |x| = -x.
  Area_1 = \int_{-2}^0 -x dx = [-\frac{x^2}{2}]_{-2}^0 = 2.
- For x \in [0, 2]: |x| = x, x|x-2| = x(2-x) = 2x - x^2. 2x - x^2 \le x \iff x - x^2 \le 0 \iff x(1-x) \le 0.
  On [0, 1]: 2x - x^2 \ge x, max is 2x - x^2.
  On [1, 2]: max is x.
  Total on [0, 3]: at x = 3, x|x-2| = 3(1) = 3 = |x|.
  Between x = 0 and x = 3: area = \frac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 3 = 4.5.
- For x \in [3, 4]: x|x-2| = x(x-2) = x^2 - 2x \ge x (since x \ge 3). So max is x^2 - 2x.
  Area_3 = \int_3^4 (x^2 - 2x) dx = [\frac{x^3}{3} - x^2]_3^4 = (\frac{64}{3} - 16) - (9 - 9) = \frac{16}{3} = 5.333.
Sum of areas = 2 + 4.5 + 5.5 = 12.
